context.requirement_text: Second requirement of S7. Ports and runs, via REQ-205's harness, the four SwiftRoute scenario YAMLs confirmed present in R-Co at tests/simulation/scenarios/: swiftroute-tenant-onboarding-happy.yaml (5 steps, all via: gui in its actual current form; DEFERRED_TO_S8 with an explicit spec-exists-but-not-integrated distinction since onboarding-wizard.pipeline.e2e.spec.ts exists in web/ but S8 integration has not started), swiftroute-shipment-high-value-happy.yaml (3 steps, all via: api, declared value EUR 750 exceeding the EUR 500 CEO co-sign threshold, exercises REQ-050's exclusive-gateway CEL/expr condition dispatch), swiftroute-shipment-ops-timeout-escalation.yaml (3 steps; step 2 needs POST /api/v1/instances/:id/advance-timer, confirmed absent by grep; record SKIP/MINOR per the scenario's own documented fallback and report the missing endpoint as a finding to ORCH per ISSUE_QUEUE.md), and swiftroute-shipment-attach-delivery-note.yaml (5 steps, all via: gui; no attachment/document-upload API exists in Letflow or in R-Co's own src/; record UNBUILT_FEATURE, zero steps executed, file as a finding). REQ-205's Runner needs two new dispositions (:skip with severity, :unbuilt_feature) added to its outcome vocabulary without breaking shipped REQ-205 code/tests.
acceptance_criteria: swiftroute-tenant-onboarding-happy's api-equivalent provisioning (tenant + admin user + realm) is exercised through REQ-205's harness (Letflow.Simulation.Seed) and its EO-001..EO-003-equivalent state is verified against real Letflow state; its gui steps are recorded DEFERRED_TO_S8 with the spec-exists-but-not-integrated distinction stated explicitly in the report

swiftroute-shipment-high-value-happy runs end to end (dispatcher submit -> ops approve -> CEO co-sign) against a real running instance and all 4 expected_outcomes are evaluated against real queried state, each recorded PASS or FAIL with the specific evidence

swiftroute-shipment-ops-timeout-escalation's step 1 and step 3 run for real; step 2 (timer advance) is recorded SKIP with severity MINOR exactly matching the scenario's own documented fallback; the missing POST /api/v1/instances/:id/advance-timer capability is reported to ORCH as a finding (not filed directly) with its file/line evidence

swiftroute-shipment-attach-delivery-note is recorded UNBUILT_FEATURE with zero steps executed, and the finding (no document/attachment API exists in Letflow or in R-Co's own src/) is reported to ORCH with the specific R-Co paths checked and found not to contain the feature

the requirement's own report states, per scenario, a closed disposition set (PASS/FAIL/SKIP/DEFERRED_TO_S8/UNBUILT_FEATURE) for every one of the four scenarios' steps -- no step is left unaddressed or silently omitted
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted

result.summary: Design written to lib/letflow/design/req206-swiftroute-scenario-execution.md. Verified this session, independently: (1) R-Co's source tree is genuinely unreachable from this sandbox (ls/find both fail), matching REQ-205's own recorded constraint -- REQ-205's already-shipped swiftroute/vortex/meridian fixtures are themselves self-authored synthetic data, not real R-Co ports, despite provenance comments citing ISS-0388; no handoff in this repo shows any session actually reading R-Co's filesystem. REQ-206's 4 scenario YAMLs must therefore also be self-authored synthetic fixtures, structurally faithful to the requirement text's own field-by-field account, under a new test/fixtures/simulation/swiftroute/scenarios/ directory, parsed by a new Letflow.Simulation.ScenarioFixture.load!/1 test-support module (the YAML->Scenario-struct parser REQ-205's own design deferred as OQ-2). (2) grep of lib/letflow/router.ex and lib/letflow/routers/*.ex for advance-timer/advance_timer: zero matches, confirming the requirement's own claim independently. (3) No attachment/upload/document route exists in any router either. (4) The already-ported process_route_approval.yaml ('Shipment Approval': ops-review -> exclusive-gateway on declared_value >/<= 500 -> ceo-approval -> release-shipment) is exactly swiftroute-shipment-high-value-happy's process -- no new process fixture needed for that scenario; process_shipment_dispatch.yaml's existing timeout-escalation shape is reused for the ops-timeout scenario. Runner extension designed as strictly additive to the shipped test/support/simulation/runner.ex: Scenario.step() gains via: :skip (third value alongside :api/:gui) plus optional severity/note fields; RunReport.step_result().outcome gains :skip as a fourth value with a mirrored severity field. Scenario gains a top-level optional unbuilt_feature: %{reason: ...} field; RunReport gains disposition: :executed | :unbuilt_feature (default :executed) and notes; run/1 gets one new leading clause that short-circuits to an all-empty report when unbuilt_feature is set, before any precondition/step/outcome machinery runs -- this keeps UNBUILT_FEATURE at scenario granularity (matching 'do not attempt to execute any of its 5 steps') distinct from :skip's step granularity. Every new field defaults to a value reproducing today's exact behavior, so all of REQ-205's shipped runner_test.exs assertions keep passing unmodified. Both undiscovered-feature findings (missing advance-timer endpoint; missing attachment subsystem) are specified as ELIXIR-DEV handoff result.issues entries for ORCH to file via register_task, per ISSUE_QUEUE.md -- ELIXIR-DEV does not call register_task itself. Five open questions recorded explicitly (§5 of the design) rather than silently resolved: which swiftroute actor stands in for the CEO role (org_structure.yaml has no role-ceo actor), whether :TasksComplete requires prior claim, the exact GET /api/v1/tasks query shape for resolving a task id post-creation, and the exact assignee_ref string Letflow.Engine writes for a role:-attributed HUMAN_TASK node. No implementation code was written -- signatures, type-shape tables, and algorithm descriptions only; verified no literal Elixir function bodies remain in the file (code fences present are shell-command transcripts, YAML fixture content, @spec lines, and issue-text templates only).
